text.en: Students in a picture measure something. Is it length, height, weight or temperature?

In this chapter students look at a picture and decide what is being measured: length, height, breadth, depth, weight or temperature.
Words like tall, wide, short and long are used in daily life. Height, width, depth and breadth all refer to measuring length.
In Class 3 we learnt that lengths are measured in metres. Check your classroom: is the height of most students more than a metre? Is your arm less than a metre? Is the door less than a metre high? Is the blackboard more than a metre wide?
1 metre is 100 centimetres. For long distances we use the kilometre: 1 kilometre is 1000 metres (additional, not in the textbook).
A ruler, a tape and a metre stick are tools to measure length.
